differences.what: Diagnostic camera only: 13 fitted points give 14.38px RMS/26.39px maximum, while five held-out upper sills retain 10–27px residuals. Fitted roll reaches +5 degrees and principal x1550.72 lies outside the chosen left exposure. This degeneracy prevents optical-calibration or photo-match acceptance.

Actual native comparison shows lower-office windows, portal bases and the front grade relation visibly too low. The roof/cornice slopes, opening positions and central apron shape also differ. Camera/geometry/grade must be reconciled jointly in a later pass; no current correction is inferred from a single fitted point.

The working cornice/roof/grade and opening proportions still disagree with pictured positions. The cameras remain preliminary; residuals and source drawing distortion do not establish a surveyed height datum.
Mansard apron shoulders, molded window crowns, cornice brackets, urns and casing profiles remain simplified. Added layers recover the main form but not the pictured carving and recesses.

The pale central roof face follows the newly inspected Carbutt photo. Its dial-like marks, precise function and finish remain unresolved; the plain face is incomplete. Upper window fanlight reflections/material appearance are also unresolved.

Basement apertures are now rectangular, as pictured, but their exposure, railing extent, street relation and some side-entrance positions remain unverified. The 2m cap is a working datum, not a source measurement.

Portal reveals now face into the aperture, with slender round shafts and capitals. Closed dark passage proxies omit visible door/threshold detail; exact entrance depth and source-specific head alignment remain open.

Stone, roof, glass and sash color/roughness are reconstructed, not measured from the monochrome/printed references. Continuous geometric stone courses recover the visible rhythm; detailed joint pattern and weathering remain unresolved.
Generic office-window bars no longer cross the triple portal. Aperture-facing reveal normals and a bounded dark backing remove the previous large pale oblique passage wedges.
Unsupported basement arches were replaced with rectangles, without changing the unresolved street datum.
Added continuous horizontal stone courses, raised roof casings attached to the mansard, and layered central apron moldings. Detailed profiles remain covered by open discrepancies.
Source neighbors, tree, poles, figures, vehicles, flags and tenant signage are outside this main-building exterior scope and do not establish October 8, 1871 continuity.
East and south elevations are outside these views and remain explicitly reconstructed. No actual city terrain contact or context-building replacement has been evaluated.
